biography.plain_text: Jon Manafort was an American construction businessman from New Britain, Connecticut. With his brother and cousin, he led the third generation of Manafort Brothers, expanding a family demolition company into civil engineering and other contracting work. He also founded Connecticut Waste Processing, starting with two trucks and developing a regional waste business.

long_biography.plain_text:
Construction businessman Jon Manafort helped establish Legend Cars racing at Stafford Motor Speedway. After racing one of the small stock cars with broadcaster Mike Joy, he discussed the class with promoter Jackie Arute. Manafort Brothers built the Mini-Mile circuit in 1994, and Jon raced alongside relatives in the family's expanding stable of cars.

Motorcycling became another shared commitment. He and his cousin Frank bought Harley-Davidsons to join the Kyle Petty Charity Ride Across America, which raised funds for Victory Junction Camp. He became a director of the charity, and his sons Jason and Justin joined the annual cross-country rides when they were old enough.
